header:
Date: 2026-09-17
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sana Reddy (Redwood CSM), Alex Moreno (Brightline Eng Manager), Priya Shah (Brightline Head of ML), Jordan Lee (Brightline CTO), Samira Khan (Brightline Security)
summary: Quarterly-ish health/check-in focused on accelerating Brightline's pilot into a short dedicated run. Topics: pilot sizing, cost tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated, SLA targets for 95th p99, security/compliance ask list, and concrete next steps for benchmark and pricing. Action items assigned and pilot timelines tentatively agreed.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Alex (Brightline): Alex here.
[00:08] Priya (Brightline): Priya here.
[00:10] Jordan (Brightline): Jordan here.
[00:12] Samira (Brightline): Samira.
[00:14] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam on the call.
[00:16] Sana (Redwood CSM): Sana here.
[00:20] Maya: Cool, objective — accelerate the pilot to a dedicated-backed run, make sure costs are understood, and that SLAs line up with your customer-facing guarantees. Priya, do you want to recap where you are with the pilot usage and target latency?
[00:30] Priya: Sure, so right now we are running on the hosted tier. Typical daily tokens about 45k but spikes to roughly 250k during peak periods when batch jobs run. Latency target for the feature is 250ms p95, p99 ideally sub 600ms. We're seeing variability esp with longer context windows, the kv cache helps but we need consistency.
[00:52] Alex: And the pilot needs to be 8 weeks, with an option to convert to reserved capacity. Our main risk is cost over time if spikes keep happening.
[01:00] Jordan: Also security — we need to ensure logs are retained only in our VPC and KMS keys are customer-managed for the dedicated run.
[01:08] Samira: Yes SOC2 report is table stakes, and we need network diagrams, encryption at rest, and the audit log cadence.
[01:15] Liam: Good callouts. For the dedicated option we can offer private deployment inside your VPC or our dedicated pool with customer-managed KMS for keys. We usually see 20-40% unit cost reductions on stable traffic when using dedicated with quantized model variants and prefix caching. But there's an up-front reservation commitment.
[01:34] Priya: Can you quantify the 20-40%? Is that for natively quantized weights or from caching/batching?
[01:40] Liam: It's a mix. For example, 8-bit quantization plus continuous batching + prefix/KV caching usually yields the lower end of that range; when traffic is predictable and caching hits are high you can hit 35-40%. We'll run a sim on your traces to show a modeled delta.
[01:54] Maya: From a commercial perspective, we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. But before that, we need the traffic traces so Liam can run a bench.
[02:03] Priya: We'll scrub PII and drop in a small sample. The tricky bit is our burst pattern — there are short high-concurrency windows that matter more than average QPS.
[02:12] Liam: Good to know. For bursts we have burst capacity policies — you can configure a burst pool and fallback routing. If dedicated saturated, we can fall back to a hosted-compatible variant with slightly higher latency but preserves availability.
[02:26] Alex: Fallback sounds good but we need deterministic behavior and an SLA on fallback latency.
[02:31] Maya: We can document a fallback SLA and offer canary windows in the pilot so you can measure it.
[02:38] Samira: Quick question on telemetry — can we get token-level cost breakdown and trace-level latency? Our ops team wants per-route cost attribution.
[02:46] Sana: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and per-route latency. We'll attach sample screenshots and the telemetry schema.
[02:53] Jordan: About compliance, will you provide an on-prem option if needed?
[02:57] Liam: We have a private deployment option and an on-prem package for air-gapped or highly regulated workloads. That path includes an extra managed deployment phase and a different support SLA. It tends to be slower but meets strict residency and control needs.
[03:12] Priya: For the pilot we prefer dedicated in our cloud account (VPC) with customer KMS. On-prem may be later.
[03:18] Maya: Understood. Let's talk success metrics: what are you measuring? Latency (p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens, and error rates?
[03:26] Alex: Yes, primary KPI p95 latency under 300ms, acceptable p99 under 700ms, cost delta vs current budget under 15% over baseline. And error rate below 0.5% for API failures.
[03:38] Liam: We'll set the benchmark test to measure those with synthetic and replayed real traces. For the replay we'll use your anonymized traces and run against both hosted and dedicated to produce apples-to-apples comparisons.
[03:49] Priya: How long will the benchmark run take?
[03:52] Liam: We can do a 24-48 hour replay to cover diurnal and burst patterns. If you want deep tails we'll do an extended 72h. The setup is a couple hours, then run and analysis the next day.
[04:06] Jordan: And cost projection accuracy — how confident is the sim? We don't want surprises mid-quarter.
[04:11] Liam: We'll give modeled ranges and a sensitivity analysis. The more representative traces you provide the tighter the band. We'll include quantization scenarios (8-bit, 4-bit) and cache-hit assumptions.
[04:22] Priya: Are there any feature toggles we should be aware of that might affect latency? For example, function calling or structured outputs?
[04:30] Maya: Yes function/tool calling adds overhead depending on the payload and sync/async patterns. We'll call that out in the benchmark and test with your common prompt patterns.
[04:38] Samira: For SOC2, please send your most recent audit and the network topology for the dedicated run. Also, do you support SAML SSO for console access?
[04:46] Sana: Yes, SAML/SSO is supported, and we'll share SOC2 and the infra diagrams.
[04:51] Alex: One more — can we define an automatic rollback policy if latency regresses? We want an automatic fallback to a more conservative model while we triage.
[04:58] Liam: Yep, Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to pre-defined compatible variants. We can attach a canary and automatic rollback window to the pilot.
[05:06] Maya: OK next steps recap: Priya send traces, Maya to send pilot pricing, Liam to schedule bench, Sana to send SOC2 and telemetry schema. Any other asks?
[05:18] Priya: No, that captures it. Quick question — timeline to convert pilot to reserved capacity?
[05:23] Maya: Typically after 6-8 weeks of pilot we do a business review; conversion depends on committed throughput and term. We'll outline options in the pricing doc.
[05:32] Jordan: Great.
[05:33] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the attachments and proposed calendar for the benchmark.
[05:39] Alex: Thanks.
[05:40] (call ends)
notes: Tone: collaborative, pragmatic. Customer risk: cost spikes during bursts and compliance requirements. Opportunity: convert pilot to reserved capacity if benchmark shows predictable savings.
questions: What's the estimated % cost reduction when moving to dedicated?
Can Redwood support customer-managed KMS and VPC deployment?
How do automatic fallbacks affect SLA guarantees?
What telemetry will be available during pilot?
